title: Superteam Earn Sponsorship Opportunity for Jabari
content:
Superteam Earn offers a platform for sponsors to connect with a network of Solana freelancers and top-tier talent across development, design, and content creation. Jabari and other project leads can post bounties to source high-quality work, ranging from Twitter threads and deep-dive essays to frontend development and UI/UX design. The platform allows sponsors to bypass traditional vetting headaches and reward contributors directly based on completed work.

  • Category: Talent Marketplace / Project Sponsorship
  • Platform: Superteam Earn
  • Reward: Varies by project brief (e.g., $500–$3,000+ depending on task type)
  • Cost to participate: Free to post (0% commission platform)
  • Eligibility: Open to crypto projects and teams seeking Solana-native talent

How to participate

  1. Navigate to the Superteam Earn sponsorship page to create a listing.
  2. Write a project brief explaining your objectives, requirements, and reward amounts.
  3. Review submissions from community builders and reward the best entries directly.

title: SSV Network Bug Bounty Program
content:
SSV Network operates a bug bounty program via Immunefi, offering rewards for identifying vulnerabilities in its decentralized validator technology infrastructure. Security researchers can earn payouts for discovering eligible smart contract security issues.

Details

  • Category: Smart Contract
  • Platform: Immunefi
  • Reward: Up to $250,000 (denominated in USD, paid in SSV)
  • Deadline: Ongoing
  • Cost to participate: Free
  • Eligibility: Open to all security researchers (KYC required for reward payout)

How to Participate

  1. Review the protocol scope, known issues, and vulnerability disclosure guidelines on Immunefi.
  2. Investigate the smart contracts and prepare a functional Proof of Concept (PoC) for any discovered bug.
  3. Submit your detailed report directly through the Immunefi platform.

title: Alibaba Unveils China’s Most Powerful AI Chip and Plans for 10-Trillion-Parameter Models
content:
On Tuesday, September 22, 2026, Alibaba Group presented a significant statement of strategic ambition at its Apsara Conference in Hangzhou. The company unveiled the Zhenwu V900, identified as China’s most powerful artificial intelligence chip to date, and outlined plans for the development of substantially larger AI models.

Developed by Alibaba’s T-Head semiconductor division, the Zhenwu V900 provides three times the performance of its predecessor, the M890. The chip features 216 GB of memory and 1,200 GB/s inter-chip bandwidth. Alibaba indicates that clusters of this new processor can scale to as many as 500,000 units to facilitate frontier-model training and inference. Mass production and commercial availability are scheduled for the first quarter of 2027.

Concurrently, CEO Eddie Wu disclosed that Alibaba’s Qwen team is already training its next-generation model, Qwen 4. Future iterations, specifically Qwen 4.5 and Qwen 5, are projected to attain 5 to 10 trillion parameters. This scale would render them approximately two to four times larger than the current flagship Qwen 3.8 Max, which possesses 2.4 trillion parameters. These expanded models are engineered for more complex, longer-horizon tasks as the company advances its pursuit of artificial superintelligence.

Furthermore, Alibaba established a long-term infrastructure objective: expanding its global Alibaba Cloud data-center capacity beyond 20 gigawatts by 2032.

These dual announcements, combining advanced domestic silicon with aggressive model scaling, highlight Alibaba’s full-stack strategy encompassing chips, models, and cloud infrastructure. These developments occur as Chinese enterprises continue to prioritize greater self-reliance in AI hardware amidst ongoing export restrictions on advanced semiconductors.

Alibaba shares increased following the announcement, reflecting investor confidence in the company’s artificial intelligence roadmap.

title: Meta Patches Zero-Day Flaw in Muse Mac App That Could Turn the AI Agent into a Backdoor
content:
Meta has released an emergency hotfix for its Muse AI assistant on macOS after security researcher Patrick Wardle discovered a zero-day vulnerability that could allow a local attacker to hijack the AI agent.

Wardle, founder of the Objective-See Foundation, disclosed the vulnerability on September 21, 2026. According to his findings, any application or terminal command running under the same user account could modify an undocumented Muse setting called "endo_voyager_dictation_endpoint".

By changing this setting, an attacker could redirect Muse's voice-dictation traffic away from Meta's servers to an endpoint controlled by the attacker.

That could expose users to several risks. An attacker could potentially capture spoken prompts, inject malicious instructions, and steal Muse authentication tokens. The situation is particularly significant because AI assistants such as Muse may have access to sensitive device capabilities, including files, the microphone, camera, location, calendars, and connected services.

Wardle released proof-of-concept code demonstrating the issue and advised users not to install the application until Meta addressed the vulnerability. He described the flaw as making it possible to turn Muse into what he called an “ultimate backdoor.”

Meta said the vulnerability was a local privilege-escalation issue, meaning it could not simply be exploited remotely over the internet. An attacker would first need the ability to execute code on the target Mac, potentially through existing malware or social engineering.

The company has since released a hotfix addressing the vulnerability and said the practical risk was limited because exploitation required local access to the device.

The discovery comes only weeks after Muse's launch and the release of its Mac application. Meta had promoted the assistant's security architecture, including isolated execution environments and a “Sentinel” system designed to reduce the impact of errors and attacks.

The incident highlights a broader security challenge surrounding increasingly powerful AI agents: the more access an AI assistant has to a user's device and services, the greater the potential impact when that assistant is compromised.

If you use the Muse Mac app, make sure you have installed the latest available update.
